content: User-facing fabro validate messages must be built as single-line format! strings (multi-line only via backslash-newline continuations verified by compilation), and the rule test must assert the EXACT expected message text, not substring containment. Substring assertions let mangled literals (embedded whitespace runs from scripted edits) pass review and ship garbled CLI output.

description: Cross-language string editing silently mangles Rust line continuations
resolution: Fixed in the fabro-900e review round: rewrote the two diagnostics in context_append_keys_within_allow.rs with real backslash-newline continuations and exact-equality assertions in the rule test (commit dc5959a80).

title: Per-node tool policy: allow-only explicit lists — no presets, no deny, no run-level list
rationale: Decided 2026-08-27 grilling for fabro-47b5 (ADR-0009 amendment). One attribute tools=<canonical names>, unset = default open. Presets are a blackbox in the graph and leak-free explicit lists self-document; deny lists cannot express read-only safely (MCP tools are run-config-dependent, future native tools leak); a run-level allowlist reintroduces replace-vs-narrow two-layer ambiguity. Presets may return later if lists grow unwieldy.

name: PermissionLevel origin: upstream interactive CLI approval axis
description: PermissionLevel (ReadOnly/ReadWrite/Full) was introduced upstream 2026-02-23 (Bryan Helmkamp, agent CLI approval callback). Enforced ONLY in the interactive CLI path via is_auto_approved(level, tool_category) at fabro-agent cli.rs ~153 (--permissions flag, default ReadWrite). Wire-contracted in OpenAPI (run events + projection). Workflow sessions report Full truthfully (no approval gating) and must never derive or remove it; tool restriction is a separate axis projected via agent_tools.

name: Upstream ownership map: tool-policy surfaces
description: Verified 2026-08-28 vs upstream/main (merge-base 56e759d47, 2026-08-26): ToolAccessPolicy/ToolAccess/ToolExposureMode + SessionOptions.tool_access_policy are upstream-owned and byte-identical in config.rs; the 'Override per-stage' comment in fabro-workflow api.rs ~1086-1089 is upstream's own words (per-stage tool attribute is their invited direction); NamedToolAccessPolicy exists upstream only as a test struct in session.rs tests; AskFabroToolAccessPolicy is upstream production pattern (canonical_tool_name matching); fabro-tool crate is upstream-owned (our only local addition: fabro_run_logs); PermissionLevel enforced only in interactive CLI (is_auto_approved, cli.rs ~153). graph.rs is our most-diverged file (204 lines from 900e+preamble work). Offer order when upstream reacts: 900e then 47b5.

name: upstream-v0.339-daytona-images-sql-line
description: Upstream v0.339.0-nightly.1 (merged 4a22e3d47, 2026-08-31): Daytona environments now accept image.docker (snapshot base image, DaytonaSnapshotSource enum in fabro-sandbox config). Fork consequence: our validate_daytona_image_settings rejection was removed as superseded; mutual-exclusion for docker provider (fabro-969f) kept in validate_docker_image_settings; from_environment.rs maps both providers through shared sandbox_dockerfile_source(). New SQL line: fabro-db migrations 2026082601_automation_run_targets, 2026082701_run_events, 2026082801_automation_environments + inactive SQL run-record store (RunSummaryStore name kept until cutover) — future state-to-SQL work must build on this line.

name: inspects-scope-defense-in-depth
description: ADR-0011 inspection scope (fabro-0c32, 5dd9ad8ca): graph attribute inspects=slug-list is the single authority declaration; it flows graph -> worker-token claim (coupled to agent:run_tools, issuance in worker_launch_spec) -> FabroRunToolServices.inspects (runner decodes own claims) -> tool registration gate + client-side target checks -> server-side per-route re-checks (RequiredAskFabroActor + target run workflow_slug; list_runs mandatory filter). Five layers, one declaration. Pattern for any future cross-workflow authority: name the capability in the graph, never the motive (inspects not revises — user decision, ADR-0011 amendment).

name: per-node-tool-policy
description: fabro-47b5 (c867a1a8): node attribute tools='read_file,grep' builds a NamedToolAccessPolicy (allow-only canonical names, profile vocab canonicalized both sides, question tools exempt both ways) threaded into SessionOptions + child SessionFactory; fabro_tools='fabro_run_get' is the inverse (default-denied opt-in overriding run.agent.fabro_tools). permission_level stays Full (wire-contracted CLI approval axis). Validation catalogs live as static lists in fabro-validate with dev-dep cross-check tests against the live crates — no production dependency edge.

title: Ask-Fabro terminal runs own sandbox liveness per turn
rationale: Session-held liveness without eviction machinery was impossible (SessionRuntimeEntry never removes entries); the projected runtime_context rebuilds conversations statelessly, so turn scope gives the no-leak guarantee of the inspection guard without a refcounted session-lifecycle system. User-facing leak (browsing finished runs, revisor fabro_ask targets) fixed with the smallest lifecycle concept that closes it.

name: interview-route-notifications
description: fabro-36d2 (789d76734): interview questions are now notifiable lifecycle events. Route key = the real event name 'interview.started' (route events lists are plain strings matched against event_name(); introducing a 'question.pending' alias would add vocabulary + a mapping layer for zero capability). Dispatch: handle_event's InterviewStarted arm calls the route-based lifecycle dispatch BEFORE the default-channel bot logic and independent of it (bot channel/dedup/state must not gate routes); route posts reuse the bot's question block language so both channels render identically. The InterviewStartedProps->Question construction is SHARED (interview_started_question) — drift between bot and route questions is impossible.

name: preamble-allow-keys-render-filter
description: fabro-e47c (7f6e32cbd): per-node preamble key scoping. The render-only allowlist filter sits in fidelity.rs before_node on the resolved context snapshot BEFORE the demote pass, so (a) node preamble AND parallel-branch preambles inherit it (both build from the same resolved copy), (b) the 16KB aggregate budget governs only the SELECTED keys. Filter rule: retain key if is_preamble_hidden_key(k) || allowlist.contains(k) — hidden engine keys pass because engine plumbing (internal.run_id, internal.parent_preamble) reads them from the resolved copy; user-visible keys are strictly governed. Wildcard: ATTR_LIST_WILDCARD='*' shared const in fabro_types::graph, used by render filter + both validate rules. Attribution evidence: --evidence-seeds fabro-e47c

name: context-key-vocabulary-foundation
description: Static context-key vocabulary (consts, prefixes, dynamic key builders, classifiers is_engine_internal_key/is_preamble_hidden_key/is_engine_stamped_key/is_engine_renderable_key) lives in fabro-types::context_keys as the SINGLE source of truth. fabro-workflow re-exports it as crate::context::keys via explicit pub use bridge (keeps 100+ call sites stable; fabro_graphviz::Fidelity re-export stays workflow-side because fabro-types has no fabro-graphviz dep). TRANSIENT_CONTEXT_KEYS is NOT on the public bridge (artifact.rs imports it qualified). Reason: fabro-validate needs the classifiers for graph lints (preamble_allow_keys_exist) but must not depend on fabro-workflow. fabro-e47c, 7f6e32cbd.

name: minimal-validateable-workflow-cli-smoke
description: Minimal CLI-validate-able workflow for smoke tests (learned via 4 failed formats in e47c cycle): directory .fabro/workflows/<name>/ with workflow.toml containing '[workflow]' table (fields: name/description/graph/metadata — NOT goal) and graph = "graph.dot" (PATH, not inline source); graph.dot needs 'digraph Name {' (nameless digraph fails the grammar), graph [goal="..."], a start node (shape=Mdiamond), an exit node (shape=Msquare or id exit/end — terminal_node rule is an ERROR not warning), and edges from start (reachability is a warning). Invoke: fabro validate <path-to-workflow.toml>.

name: cross-run-worker-authorization-extractor
description: UPDATED for v0.344.0-nightly.0 (3f6681b26): the RequireRunManagementTarget ancestry walk no longer uses Database::get_cached_summary (removed upstream); it reads state.stores.run_summaries.get(&run_id, Utc::now()) — the SQLite read model (authoritative post-cutover, better than a warm cache for authorization). Sandbox inspection reconnects use AppState::cached_run_projection() (Arc<RunProjection>). Boundary tests unchanged (run_tool_worker_cross_run_routes_require_inspects_scope, ancestor isolation, cyclic chain). New invariant to watch: CachedRunProjection wraps Arc<RunProjection> and SQL created_at derives from run_id.created_at() — encode timestamps in RunIds in tests.

name: engine-registered-stage-tool
description: fabro-e804 (6890362b3): workflow-registered stage tools follow the fabro_run_tool closure pattern extended with per-node state: a RegisteredTool executor closes over Arc<ContextReadState> (RwLock view + run-scoped run_store/sandbox/run_dir + tokio Mutex locality); services flow per-node through CodergenRunRequest (built in Handler::execute where resolved wf_context, node, graph, and services.run are all in scope); CachedAgentSession AND LiveAgentInvocation carry the state handle so a reused full-fidelity thread refreshes per node and a mid-run failover swaps session+handle together. Registration is default-open in create_session_for for parent profile AND the subagent factory; NamedToolAccessPolicy (tools=) is the exclusion. Values over the shared artifact::resolve_inline_max_bytes threshold demote via the same machinery as preambles; serve() defensively rehydrates surviving blob:// refs via resolve_json_value. Test graphs: build programmatically (Graph::new + Node::new + AttrValue::Integer for int attrs) - DOT strings fail the parser and String('2') is not int_attr.

name: scoped-sandbox-decorator
description: fabro-ba96 (b312459b4): per-node filesystem scope fs_hide/fs_write enforced by a ScopedSandbox decorator wrapping the stage session's Arc<dyn Sandbox> at workflow session construction (next to node.tools()). Covers every file tool in every vocabulary, read_many_files and apply_patch for free; subagent factory gets the same wrap (inheritance). Nonexistent semantics: hidden = reads fail, file_exists false, grep/glob/list_dir/walk_files filtered, writes denied; a dir/** glob also hides the dir entry (pure-glob semantics would leak the directory through listings). apply_patch pre-checks all target paths via ToolContext.fs_scope (atomic reject, no partial application). delegate_sandbox! cannot skip overridden methods — the impl is hand-written; macro evolution only when a second decorator appears (seed 922f).

fs_globs_valid test asserted fixed diagnostic indices over graph.nodes.values() — but Graph.nodes is a HashMap with per-process random iteration order, so the test passed by luck and failed after an unrelated rewrite. Any new validate rule test asserting multi-node diagnostic ORDER must sort or use order-independent any()-assertions (established pattern: tools_requires_agent_node sorts node_ids).
resolution: Made the test order-independent (sort messages, any()-assertions).

description: gate script bug class: nu parse nesting + external spread word-split; exercise all paths locally
resolution: Fixed in c0b22f39d + locally exercised gate paths; guard rule: full local gate run before pushing gate changes

content: Markdown table cells in agent preambles must be sanitized single-line: newlines -> ' / ', blank/indent runs collapsed, literal '|' escaped as '\|' (see sanitize_table_cell in lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/llm/preamble.rs). Bullet-list renderings (append_filtered_context/append_large_value) intentionally keep multi-line output; only the summary:high '## Current context' table path sanitizes. Never change format_value globally.

name: evidence-nu-diff-walk-included-append
description: evidence.nu diff-walk invariant: a file is appended to 'included' as soon as git diff exits 0 — BEFORE the empty-text check — so files with zero per-seed hunks are silently skipped but never disclosed as cap-omitted. When refactoring or reusing the walk (e.g. loop-diff-section, fabro-4b57), preserve that append placement; hoisting it after the empty check would list every hunk-less file under 'hard cap hit' and change seed-section output (fabro-4b57 verified via scratch-repo scenarios: churn-only emits loop-work diff, mixed stays counts-only).

name: partial-success-create-then-start
description: Partial-success reporting for create-then-start tool calls (fabro-78ac, lib/components/fabro-tool/src/create.rs): when an operation creates a durable resource and a follow-up call fails, return Ok with the resource id plus an additive Option<String> error field (start_error) on the structured result instead of ?-propagating — the LLM caller otherwise retries and duplicates the resource. Report the failure verbatim (e.g. 'start blocked: approval_required') and use status 'unknown' rather than guessing 'pending'; keep genuine create/parent-resolution failures as Err since nothing was created. Text summary adds 'start blocked for N' so it never implies a clean start.

Gate RED from rustfmt alignment in new test fixtures (fabro-78ac run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN): hand-aligned struct-literal fields in mod tests drift from pinned-nightly rustfmt. Fix: run 'cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt -p <crate>' after editing test fixtures instead of hand-aligning columns.
resolution: Reformatted lib/components/fabro-tool with pinned nightly rustfmt; fmt --check now clean

description: fabro-tool clippy gate red: nightly clippy denies map_unwrap_or and format_push_string; use map_or_else and write! into the String (std::fmt::Write) instead of push_str(&format!(..)) — seen in create.rs partial-success fix, run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN
resolution: rewrote both sites; clippy -D warnings and all 67 fabro-tool tests green

name: long-poll-client-bypasses-control-plane-timeout
description: Pattern: transport-level exceptions to the shared request timeout get their own send variant — send_api_long_poll in lib/foundation/fabro-client/src/client.rs mirrors send_api (classification + token refresh) minus the timeout wrapper; documented 'keep in sync with send_api'. Client::wait_run is the only caller. If another long-poll endpoint appears, reuse the variant rather than bypassing timeouts ad hoc.

name: pending-approval-expiry-transition-table
description: When introducing a new terminal failure reason: (1) add the enum variant, (2) EXTEND can_transition_to in fabro-types status.rs for every source status that can reach it, (3) update the contract test that pins per-reason transition expectations, (4) align the OpenAPI FailureReason enum (it had drifted: deadlock/soft_stop were missing). Symptom of a missed arm: append_event rejects with 'invalid status transition'.

Upstream merges must gate with clippy --all-targets + nextest on touched crates, not the qualitygate's compile-only workspace fallback: the v0.347 squash-merge gate (cargo check only) let fork lint/snapshot debt through (large_futures at runner.rs:1021, unused_async in run_wait.rs, missing approval_timeout_secs in attach/inspect snapshots), which surfaced on the next merge.
resolution: v0.348 merge pass fixed all three debt items and ran the full gate (clippy workspace all-targets clean, 4465/4465 nextest green); conflict-policy.md 2026-09-06 section codifies running the deeper gate every merge

content: Rerun nextest only after 'touch <changed-file>' when a snapshot or test-source fix appears not to take effect; identical failure line numbers across runs indicate a stale binary, not a bad fix. Observed twice in the v0.348.0-nightly.0 upstream merge (attach.rs, inspect.rs).

description: Any supervisor whose JoinHandle serve.rs awaits MUST race its interval against state.shutdown_token().cancelled() (tokio::select!, MissedTickBehavior::Delay) — the pull_request_supervisor loop is the canonical template. A polled is_shutting_down() flag after a long tick breaks server stop. Regression class caught only by tests that spawn real servers; the gate run also exposed that focused clippy needs --features test-support to lint fabro-server it-targets (workspace runs unify the feature via the fabro-auth dev-dependency).
resolution: Fixed in 762832197: select-loop against shutdown token; worker_auth tests pass in ~1s; verified via clippy with --features test-support.

name: automation-breaker-high-water-baseline
description: Automation circuit breaker (fabro-3d97): per-trigger counters are store-backed with a last-processed-run high-water mark (automation_triggers.breaker_* columns); on first observation or after a replace (the enable path rewrites trigger rows) the newest terminal run becomes the baseline WITHOUT counting, which is what makes 'resume resets the counter' work — a stateless tail-count would instantly re-pause after re-enable. Also: run_summaries.list_all/list_terminal_for_automation return NEWEST-FIRST; scheduler tests must sort by created_at before indexing runs by fire order.

fabro-server graph-render unit tests (server::tests::get_graph_returns_svg, render_graph_from_manifest_*) spawn 'fabro __render-graph' resolved via current_exe().parent().parent()/fabro (target/debug/fabro). The touched-crates qualitygate (scripts/qualitygate.nu) only builds/clippies touched crates, so when a run touches fabro-server without fabro-cli the binary is absent and these 3 tests fail deterministically (run 01M1VZTJSZ551NFPHPXD429MG0, tester stage).
resolution: Build 'cargo build -p fabro-cli --bin fabro' before gating fabro-server; root fix belongs in the gate (build the fabro bin when fabro-server is touched).

description: Whenever a migration file is added on a branch switch or cache reuse and behavior says 'column/migration missing': suspect the embedded MIGRATOR, not the DB. Diagnosis: query _sqlx_migrations (with -wal!) for the newest version. Mitigations: touch lib/foundation/fabro-db/src/lib.rs before just up after migration changes (until fabro-db gains rerun-if-changed in build.rs, filed as seed); cargo clean -p fabro-db for local test binaries. Deep lesson: /health + one API roundtrip is not deploy verification — the new automations smoke probe exists because the broken surface had no probe.
resolution: Smoke probe landed (authenticated automations check, live-proofed red on the broken deploy); build.rs hardening filed as P1 seed; deploy-watch-5 verifies the volume-cache rebuild.

name: sqlx-migrate-rerun-if-changed
description: Crates embedding sqlx::migrate! need a build.rs emitting cargo:rerun-if-changed=migrations (and =build.rs); cargo fingerprints do not reliably invalidate on migration file add/remove under local-target and docker-volume caches, shipping a stale MIGRATOR (fabro-bc9b). Pair with a unit test asserting max(MIGRATOR versions) equals max version parsed from the on-disk migrations dir via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, and log the newest embedded version at migrate() startup.

Run-stage scripts invoking mise-wrapped commands (just qualitygate, sd) fail with 'Config files in /repos/denkhaus/fabro/.mise.toml are not trusted' whenever the sandbox/home is recycled or .mise.toml changes, killing the whole stage before any code runs (run 01M1XCHJTDBJKZ31VFMY1KD61Q tester stage).
resolution: Immediate: 'mise trust /repos/denkhaus/fabro/.mise.toml' once per environment (done this session). Durable: stage bootstrap or justfile entry should export MISE_YES=1 or pre-trust before invoking mise-dependent recipes.

name: autonomous-run-failure-triage
description: autonomous-run failure triage: 'fabro ps -a --json' (full ULIDs) + run-detail API gives lifecycle.status.reason (soft_stop / cancelled / workflow_error / stall watchdog); the authoritative per-run evidence is the engine log inside the deployed server container: docker exec fabro-fabro-1 cat /storage/scratch/<YYYYMMDD>-<runid>/runtime/server.log — grep for 'ERROR|Workflow run failed|watchdog|cancel'. API needs auth: bearer token from ~/.fabro/auth.json servers entry (dev-token). Stage-journal jsonl in .fabro/journal/ lags until the run's PR merges, so server.log is the live source. Validated 2026-09-07: root-caused 11 failed passes (stall watchdog vs blocking fabro_run_wait, zai 5h quota soft-stop, pass-guard cancels) in minutes.

title: engine stays tool-agnostic about project-scope tooling
rationale: User decision 2026-09-07 (fabro session, grill on fabro-66db): mise and any other project-scope tool exists only in the project's own artifacts; the fabro engine (sandbox providers, workflow engine, server, CLI) must stay tool-agnostic. A first fix that ran 'mise trust' inside docker.rs/daytona providers was reverted unmerged - layering violation. Project tooling bootstrap lives in project artifacts: .fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain (ENV MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS=/repos/*/*/.mise.toml - trust-by-glob, content-independent, verified in mise 2026.8.10), server environment env config, or workflow hooks. The engine's stable contract for bootstrap purposes is the clone layout /repos/<owner>/<repo> + /workspace/<repo> symlink. Full decision: ADR-0017 docs/lab/adr/0017-engine-stays-tool-agnostic-about-project-scope-tooling.md. Rule also anchored in AGENTS.md (sandbox section) and the iterate skill standing rules.

description: Edit-tool writes can land with epoch-0 (1970-01-01) mtimes; cargo then considers the source older than cached artifacts and silently skips recompiles, so binary behavior lags source edits (hit while iterating the fabro-validate bin in run 01M1Y2SMEVDHAFB59GZV9B84CQ: import of a just-added pub fn failed until manually touching the file). After surprising stale-behavior, touch the edited .rs files before rebuilding.
resolution: Touch edited source files before rebuild when a just-added symbol is reported missing or behavior seems stale.

name: standalone-graph-lint-preprocessing
description: Standalone workflow-graph linting (scripts/validate-workflows.nu + fabro-validate bin, seed fabro-513e): raw graphs must be preprocessed exactly like the runtime pipeline before lint rules run — resolve @-prefixed prompt/goal refs against the graph dir (missing files left for unresolved_file_ref) and blank template-syntax model_stylesheet (runtime renders it before stylesheet_syntax; raw MiniJinja source is unlintable). Any new pre-render transform added to the pipeline needs a matching preprocessing step here or the standalone gate false-positives.

Stale cargo test binary after edit_file changes: nextest reused a prior compile whose fingerprints did not register the edit (run 01M1YBBXR99PNME6Y8ZED4Y2NN, fabro-fb16) — panic line numbers pointed 7-14 lines away from the actual asserts and two tests failed on a code path the source no longer contained.
resolution: touch the edited file (or cargo test --no-run) to force recompilation before trusting a failure diagnosis; after the forced rebuild both tests passed unchanged.

name: tar-upload-mtime
description: Docker sandbox single-file tar uploads (build_single_file_tar in lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/docker.rs) must set header mtime via SystemTime::now before set_cksum; a zero/epoch mtime makes extracted container files land at 1970-01-01 so cargo treats sources as older than cached rlibs and silently skips recompiles after agent edits (fabro-22e4).

Seed fabro-22e4's mtime-0 bug is live in the agent tooling itself: after edit_file writes, lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/push_credentials.rs carried mtime 1970-01-01, so cargo check replayed stale dead-code warnings from the cached fingerprint instead of recompiling (run 01M1YJ8R820R7ZMSN55GJGMZ4A, implementer re-pass). Symptom: warnings citing line numbers that no longer match edited source. Workaround while the docker transport fix propagates: touch touched .rs files (or find lib -name '*.rs' ! -newermt 2000-01-01) before cargo check/clippy. Also fixed the gate-blocking default-feature compile: mod managed_labels was cfg-gated behind docker/daytona/test while pub use managed_labels::RUN_ID_LABEL stayed ungated (introduced 4c1ca7e); push_credentials.rs needed matching cfg gates on build_token_source, the first PushCredentialState impl, and three imports to satisfy -D warnings under default features.
resolution: Docker transport fix landed in e6ae814 (build_single_file_tar stamps wall-clock mtime); until the rebuilt binary reaches every sandbox, touch edited sources before cargo invocations to force recompilation.

name: gh-auth-via-tool-env-not-image
description: gh auth in run containers needs no image-side credentials: fabro-workflow services.rs resolve_workflow_env injects a freshly minted GITHUB_TOKEN into the agent tool env per shell call (fabro-agent ToolEnvProvider), and gh reads GITHUB_TOKEN natively — so baking the gh binary into fabro-toolchain (aqua:cli/cli pin in .fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain, fabro-05d0) is sufficient for the planner's 'gh pr list --state open' in-flight-PR guard.

title: gh verboten in Agent-Sandboxen: ADR-0019 Capability Gate
rationale: gh was briefly baked into the toolchain image (PR #53, fabro-05d0) and REVERTED (f00fdb102, user decision 2026-09-08). Why gh is FORBIDDEN in agent sandboxes: the engine injects a freshly minted GITHUB_TOKEN into every agent shell call (fabro-workflow services.rs resolve_workflow_env) plus a git credential bridge (git_bridge.rs credential helper reads $GITHUB_TOKEN at invocation time). gh + that token = fully write-capable forge client in agent shells (merge, close, force-push, branch delete) bypassing every engine governance control (gate, revisor, auto-merge). fabro-github (server-side crate) is the ONLY sanctioned forge write path - agents express intent via mediated tools (fabro_run_create/wait/get), the engine executes. Direct agent tools are read-only at most; extend existing tools over adding new ones; capability changes in agent-reachable surfaces are needs-user decisions. Open-PR visibility for the planner guard comes from fabro_runs_list (Weg A, fabro-06e0), never from a forge client. Full rule: ADR-0019.

title: Line workflows run tokenless - lab-era GITHUB_TOKEN permissions removed
rationale: Follow-up to the gh incident (ADR-0019, user directive 2026-09-08): develop/revisor/merge-upstream carried contents=write + pull_requests=write since the world merger (d9138572c, lab-era heritage) - injecting a write-capable forge token into every agent shell (engine resolve_workflow_env is OPT-IN: empty permissions = no_token). Removed in dd5cd294c after verifying zero shell consumers in the line (no git push, no gh; the engine does all forge ops with its own push_credentials). code-review/gh-list/gh-triage keep explicit scoped integrations (manual workflows needing them). Acceptance signal: next line passes' shells have NO GITHUB_TOKEN; closeout/seeds-sync unaffected (local commits, engine pushes run branches). If a future workflow needs forge access, it must declare scoped permissions AND pass the ADR-0019 capability gate (needs-user).

content: Terminal workflow nodes (shape Msquare / exit) never dispatch a Handler: fabro-core executor.rs short-circuits them via on_terminal_reached. Test capture points must live on non-terminal nodes (e.g. wait/insulator with duration=1ms).

name: server-seam-wire-test-without-docker
description: create_run_with_bearer_for_graph + issue_test_run_tools_worker_token produce Worker-principal runs through the real HTTP API; dev-user bearer (auto-injected by build_test_router) provides the User-principal differential.

fabro-server tests that execute runs in-process with default settings resolve the seeded 'default' environment (Docker provider) and hard-fail with WorkflowError 'Socket not found: /var/run/docker.sock' in Docker-less gate sandboxes (run 01M20T9S8JRXETASN64768TRRP: fabro-e505/fabro-c274 bridge tests). Pin such tests to the reserved local environment via '[run.environment] id = "local"' in the test TOML — Normal mode keeps real handler dispatch, unlike mode = "dry_run" which routes handlers to simulate() and silently skips execute-path assertions (empty observation vectors).
resolution: Both bridge tests pinned to id = "local"; full fabro-server suite 929/929 green without Docker; gate now environment-independent

content: Set [run.clone] depth = 0 in workflow.toml for any workflow whose stages run git rev-list --count or git merge-base across origin and upstream remotes; verify with git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository in the sandbox when counts look inflated.

name: run-clone-depth-zero-for-range-math
description: Workflows doing git range math against upstream (rev-list --count, merge-base) need [run.clone] depth = 0 in their .fabro/workflows/<name>/workflow.toml; default depth-100 shallow clone breaks the math. Conductor (a4850e681) and merge-upstream (fabro-85a1) both set it; audit any new clone-based workflow that compares upstream refs. Volume is ~neutral (~150 MB either way).

title: FabroRunToolServices presence vs run_wide provenance
rationale: The worker-token agent:run_tools scope is granted for both the run-wide flag and node-level fabro_tools opt-ins, so services presence alone can no longer decide whether attribute-less stages get the full tool set; provenance must travel with the services to keep per-stage least privilege (ADR-0019, user-approved Option A on fabro-c419).

name: overlap-guard-live-children
description: Overlap guard (on_overlap=skip) must treat non-terminal CHILD runs of an automation's runs as active, not only non-terminal automation runs: a conductor pass that parks at a boundary exit or soft-stops via a misjudged run_wait (fabro-ee5d) is terminal itself while its develop child still runs — that window admitted a second overlapping pass (fabro-91ff incident, PR #84 vs #86). active_run_for_automation in lib/components/fabro-store/src/run_summary_store.rs matches parent automation_id OR parent_id IN automation runs with status NOT IN (succeeded,failed,dead); also note the develop planner in-flight guard now needs run STATUS (running) not just open PRs, since claims precede PRs by ~15 min.

name: routing-schema-label-constraint
description: Routing output_schema label constraint (fabro-de4d): OutputSchemaKind::Routing carries allowed_labels derived from the node's unconditional outgoing edge labels (routable_edge_labels in structured_output.rs); parse_node_output_schema takes (graph, node) and CodergenRunRequest/OneShotRequest carry &Graph so backend repair loops enforce the constraint. Unknown preferred_next_label fails the OUTPUT with SchemaValidation kind (verbose: names value + full allowed list, normalized via graph::routing::normalize_label for case/accelerator insensitivity). Empty edge set keeps free-form drop semantics. Graph lint routing_fallback_silent warns on unlabeled unconditional catchers.

name: run-event-variant-touchpoints
description: Adding a run-event variant (fabro-94e8 pull_request.closed): seven touchpoints — fabro-types misc.rs Props + run_event/mod.rs EventBody variant/name/round-trip test, fabro-workflow event/events.rs variant+trace, names.rs, convert.rs, fabro-store run_state.rs reducer arm; EventBody is serde(tag=event,content=properties) so Unknown fallback makes it wire-compatible without migrations.

title: adr-0020-node-tools-reviewer-gated
rationale: User decision 2026-09-09 grill: an engine-side read-only allowlist would split the capability model and make the overall logic harder to explain without removing the trust question; the reviewer is the instance that can best judge 'what the task minimally requires' and must recognize and block unjustified escalations. Run-wide flag remains the only widener for attribute-less stages; new tools stay full ADR-0019 item-4 user decisions.

description: resolve_pr_model (lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/operations/start.rs) only falls back to the run model for bare provider tokens / ambiguous refs; a provider-QUALIFIED unknown selector (e.g. zai:nonexistent-model) passes through resolve_selection which echoes the selector as the model id, so the PR-body call would fail at client time instead of falling back to the run model. Found while writing fabro-6a5a tests; documented via resolve_pr_model_falls_back_to_run_model_for_bare_provider.
resolution: Not fixed (out of fabro-6a5a scope): documented via the bare-provider fallback test; the qualified-unknown-selector passthrough is journal-reported for a future seed.

title: Mixed-capture evidence: anomaly section for loop paths changed alongside seed work
rationale: PR #109 flipped auto_merge=false across three workflow.toml files and was approved because the evidence capture demoted loop-path changes to counts-only churn whenever seed work existed — the reviewer never saw the diff. Detection is cheaper and safer than classification: fabro-93a7 (spec-named path promotion) and fabro-9d2f (worktree-diff quarantine) stay open separately.

name: lifecycle-two-reducer-equivalence-via-shared-table
description: Proving server live fold and store RunProjectionReducer agree is done transitively (fabro-3fe4): one pure table fabro_types::apply_lifecycle_event consumed by BOTH, plus two thin equivalence tests (xorshift property test durable-reducer-vs-table in run_state.rs::lifecycle_equivalence, and live_lifecycle_status-vs-table step test in fabro-server server/tests.rs). Live-only guards (RunRunnable ingestion suppression) are documented deviations in the step test, not table arms. Historic pre-table stream shapes (Submitted->Starting jumps, fast-forwarded RunFailed) live in fabro_types::historic_skipped_statuses so the shim has one owner and the table stays strict.

fabro-3fe4 reopen (runs 01M25K41V4NE, 01M25R832HP): making the live reducer strictly apply the shared lifecycle table stranded injected event sequences (submitted + worker-shaped run.starting, RunRunnable suppressed by the scheduling guard) at Submitted, so fabro rm no longer saw terminal runs as completed and failed dogfood-gate. Lesson: when two reducers share one strict table, any per-reducer guard (RunRunnable suppression) must be paired with the shared fast-forward path, or live/durable status drift breaks downstream terminality predicates like requires_force_to_delete.
resolution: Shared helper fabro_types::historic_skipped_statuses consumed by BOTH live_lifecycle_status (server.rs) and RunProjectionReducer (run_state.rs); rm completed-run tests pass on final tree.

description: checkpoint.completed run event exceeds MAX_RUN_EVENT_BODY_BYTES (3MB) on big merge-upstream runs: worker loses canonical run store (HTTP 413) AFTER the merge commit exists, run is marked failed(workflow_error), conductor pass soft-stops, and the merge work is stranded in the sandbox (fabro/run/* pushes rejected by GitHub branch protection, nothing persisted remotely). Observed 2026-09-11 on runs 01M27V69 and 01M2837. Salvage: docker start the stopped run container, docker cp .git out, fetch into host repo, push under salvage/<name> (fabro/run/* blocked, salvage/* allowed).
resolution: Unresolved: needs code fix — bound checkpoint event payload size (blob-store large data like tool outputs already do via MAX_SERIALIZED_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES) or raise MAX_RUN_EVENT_BODY_BYTES; independently allow-list fabro/run/* pushes so finished work is persisted before sandbox teardown. Interim manual salvage procedure documented in description.

name: sqlite-busy-classification-and-wal-test-pools
description: SQLite BUSY resilience in fabro-store run-event writes (fabro-3ef7): sqlx surfaces the EXTENDED error code via DatabaseError::code() (e.g. 517 SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT), so busy classification must mask to the primary code (code & 0xff == 5) plus a 'database is locked' message fallback; and file-backed test pools must set journal_mode(Wal) to mirror the canonical fabro-db connect policy — rollback-journal test pools deadlocked forever (not code-5) when two same-process pools held overlapping write transactions, silently failing to reproduce the production incident.

title: Long-window rate limits: parse reset prose, fail fast, park as SoftStop
rationale: Count-based exponential backoff cannot bridge multi-hour provider usage windows; burning retry attempts then failing hard left runs unrecoverable (fabro-a3d8 evidence). The reset deadline arrives only in 429 message prose, so fabro-llm parses it, attaches it as the structured provider_retry_after field, lets the lithos retry_after_cap surface the error immediately, and the workflow parks the run as FailureReason::SoftStop which stays resumable.

title: Sandbox layer rides the driver; fork seams are tool-layer scope + lifecycle guards
rationale: Upstream #849 deleted every substrate our sandbox-layer features were built on (trait, bollard, daytona SDK). Re-implementing them in fabro would fight the platform direction; the surviving seams are the agent tool layer (fs scope), request/turn-scoped lifecycle guards (upstream still leaks), and deploy-time/provider-owned image provisioning.

title: Structured-output size overflow recovers, never parks (fabro-274d)
rationale: A revisor-like stage whose findings JSON exceeds the provider output cap is not a correctness defect in the model's answer; parking the run deterministically loses drafted work. Truncation (unterminated outermost JSON object) gets length-aware repair and a best-effort persist with an explicit marker + run.notice; only balanced-but-invalid outputs keep the deterministic failure.

title: Line recovery: quota parks + fixed 10-minute recheck (ADR-0021)
rationale: Every recovery path ended in an external flip after the zai 5h hard-cut; the user demanded server-autonomous recovery with fixed 10-minute rechecks and no prose-parsed backoff (zai sends offset-less wallclocks).

description: Run 01M2E7VZYX8V forensics: zai 5h hard-cut surfaced as deterministic goal-gate failure (5 retries burned against the closed window, then the goal gate errored), and the conductor died by the 1800s stall watchdog DURING a legal 60m fabro_run_wait. Terminal signatures lied about the cause.
resolution: ADR-0021 landed 2026-09-14: park classification stops retry burn and goal-gate masking; loop graphs pin stall_timeout=63m so legal 60m waits survive the watchdog.

name: retry-continuation-seam
description: Retry-as-continuation seam (fabro-183f): the executor's attempt context crosses the handler boundary as fabro_core::handler::AttemptInfo { attempt, prior_failure } — NodeHandler::execute and workflow Handler::execute take it as a last param; only AgentHandler consumes it (others take _attempt). PebbleBackend parks a retryably-failed conversation via export_for_reuse under the thread key (or the stage-id key when threadless; stage ordinals are stable across attempts via StageExecutionTracker::ensure) and sends continuation_message() instead of re-posting the prompt; a resumed execution learns it supersedes a prior one from the lifecycle-seeded internal.stage_resumed_from context key (transient, cleared at node boundaries). httpmock note: mocks match first-created-first, so overlapping matchers need mutually exclusive body_includes/body_excludes.

Gate-red root cause (run 01M2G27BSCZSP0NASEVMH36PB9): the two fabro-server bridge tests (run_start_grants_github_token_bridge_only_to_user_principals, worker_principal_run_without_vault_token_takes_no_token_path) were the recurring 'Docker-socket failures' — they were the only tests driving a real in-process workflow to completion with the DOCKER-seeded default test environment, so any daemon-free gate environment fails them with 'Failed to build sandbox: Socket not found /var/run/docker.sock' before any handler dispatch. Verified pre-existing on the parent commit.
resolution: New test_app_state_with_runtime_settings_environment_and_registry_factory helper seeds LOCAL provider; bridge_intent_run switches the intent target to a leaked tempdir folder target because admission rejects none-targets on non-clone providers ('none targets require a compatible Docker or Daytona environment'). Both tests pass daemon-free; bridge observations unchanged.

description: just verify implementer (scripts/verify.nu, fabro-6e7f) is broken on nu 0.115.0: line 41 uses parse --regex with an interpolated string $'...' whose (?P<sha>...) group is parsed as a nushell subexpression, so the ONE mechanical implementer verification call fails with a parse error before any check runs. Fix idea: use a plain single-quoted string for the regex (no $'...' interpolation needed there). Observed run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC.
resolution: unresolved: loop-asset path, report-don't-fix applied; implementer fell back to the manual per-crate policy (fmt+clippy green, test-file-touched suites green)

description: Semantics change in fabro-tool inherit_parent_target (fabro-b4ed, run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC) passed the implementer's crate-scoped verify but red-lined the tester: the fabro-server integration fixture lib/apps/fabro-server/src/run_tool_create.rs builds a parent via test_run_spec() whose pull_request settings stay None, so under the new option-(a) semantics the child correctly inherits the base branch and the checkout assertion reads 'original'. Lesson: any change to inherited-target semantics must update downstream fixture parents to enable pull_request settings when the test means to exercise run-branch chaining. Also: after editing a src-integrated test file, confirm nextest actually recompiled — a stale binary reported the pre-edit panic line.
resolution: Fixture parent now sets pull_request enabled before inherit, matching the new chaining precondition; test passes and full fabro-server suite is green (939/939).

name: rest-only-github-conflict-resolution
description: PR staleness supervisor conflict resolution (fabro-895d): implement GitHub-side conflict handling purely through REST (compare base...head + head...base intersection for conflicting paths, contents API with Accept: application/vnd.github.raw for file bodies, git blobs/trees/commits + PATCH git/refs for the merge push) instead of local git clones — the whole resolution stays httpmock-wire-testable in fabro-server tests.rs with no git binary or protocol mocking. Parking (leave PR open, stop attempts) uses an in-memory StalePrState.parked map beside the strike counters.

name: stranded-run-salvage-via-checkpoint-branch
description: Salvage pattern for stranded runs (2026-09-15, run 01M2J1BA2J): a terminal-failed run carries its full work in the committed checkpoint branch (origin/fabro/run/<id>, sha = final_git_commit_sha from run.failed). Salvage = fetch the branch, cherry-pick the implementer commit onto current denkhaus, adapt to whatever landed in between (here: v0.356 billing->usage rename; compiler E0559/E0425 lists every fixture site), then fork-pin per policy BEFORE merging so the next upstream merge cannot drop the feature. Verify the cherry-pick compiles immediately: textual auto-merge success says nothing about type renames.

Run-history activation crash-loop diagnosis recipe (2026-09-15, netcup-5): nightly crash-loop with exit 1 + 'stored run summary ... inconsistent field summary_json' means schema-era divergence between stored rows and the replayed projection. Reproduce offline: scp the fabro-storage volume, patch diag_replay_real_run_and_diff_summary_json to loop SELECT id FROM runs (or generalize to FABRO_DIAG_RUN), run FABRO_DIAG_DB=<copy> cargo nextest run -p fabro-store diag_replay_real_run — it prints every divergent JSON pointer per run. Cost equality check across rows proves whether a verify strip masks real drift. Full E2E before release: copy the whole /storage volume, run target/debug/fabro server start with FABRO_STORAGE_DIR/FABRO_HOME/FABRO_CONFIG pointing at the copy and SESSION_SECRET from gopass — install mode means FABRO_CONFIG did not resolve.
resolution: fix efa4a493f: era-gated billing/usage strip in verify_run_json_field + flat billing event normalizers in fork_legacy_read + decode lift; validated 38 runs / 21034 events against prod copy and live on netcup-5 (image 0.357.0-nightly.0-efa4a493f)

title: Quarantine failed-stage worktree residue at GitLifecycle::on_checkpoint
rationale: A steered/failed stage's abandoned diff otherwise gets committed by a later cycle's checkpoint (git add -A), attributing dead work to a live seed; reverting residue at the failed stage's own cycle boundary keeps checkpoints scoped to the completing stage.

description: nu's rm -rf refuses to delete a directory containing the current cwd ('Cannot remove any parent directory'), so a fixture battery that cd's into a scratch dir must cd back to a saved $env.PWD in a finally block before cleanup. Hit while writing .fabro/scripts/dup-run-check-fixtures.nu (fabro-4b76): all assertions passed but the script exited 1 from the cleanup rm alone.
resolution: Save $env.PWD at entry and cd back inside finally before rm -rf; battery now exits 0.

description: Stale test-binary near-miss (run 01M2NP2W92HHF3QAH17F42GZ5K, seed fabro-b959): after edit_file changes to lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/automation_scheduler.rs, a cargo nextest run reported a panic at a source line whose content no longer matched the panic message — cargo had not rebuilt (0.5s Finished, test binary reused), so a correct fix evaluated as still failing for two runs.
resolution: Check panic line/content against current source before re-deriving root cause; force touch + rebuild when inconsistent

title: Automation-lag watchdog arms (fabro-79d8)
rationale: The seed demanded the watchdog not alert while an env update is in flight, but fabro-server has no durable marker for that state; last_error is the closest loud-line signal and keeps the change minimal (scheduler file only).

name: agent-run-attribution-header
description: Agent-run attribution marker (fabro-3916): run-create requests may carry X-Fabro-Agent-Session header; server seam is run_provenance/agent_attributed_subject in fabro-server handler/runs.rs which re-labels ONLY authenticated Principal::User subjects as Principal::Agent{session_id}. Declared in OpenAPI components/parameters/AgentSessionHeader on POST /runs; progenitor generates builder .x_fabro_agent_session(); fabro-client wraps it as create_run_from_intent_with_agent_session; CLI flag --agent-session on RunArgs. Note: openapi-generator TS regen needs Java which the run sandbox lacks — generated TS client was hand-edited generator-equivalently (4 createRun sites in runs-api.ts).

Adding a clap flag to shared run args in lib/apps/fabro-cli/src/args.rs breaks two inline help snapshots (tests/it/cmd/create.rs and tests/it/cmd/run.rs help tests). cargo-insta is NOT installed in the run sandbox, so update the inline snapshots directly from the nextest failure diff. Run 01M2P22VYWQNJM64D15XPHFP2C: tester gate red on exactly these two tests.
resolution: Inserted the missing --agent-session line into both inline help snapshots directly from the nextest failure diff; both tests and the full fabro-cli suite green

description: Nushell footguns in fabro command-node scripts: (1) 'path self' is parse-time-only — using it inside a def body passes 'nu -c use' parse checks but fails at runtime; assign 'const DIR = (path self | path dirname)' at top level instead. (2) Context keys that contain a literal dot (engine 'output.<node>' keys) cannot be nested-accessed: dotted member access raises column-not-found and lookup_flat's dotted walk cannot reach inside them; use get 'output.preflight' instead — edge conditions must therefore route on preferred_label, never on fields inside an output.<node> object. (3) mut vars typed by their null initializer reject later non-null assignment — initialize with a typed placeholder. Found implementing fabro-a32f (planner-preflight.nu + fixtures).
resolution: Const anchors for path self; quoted-key get for dotted context keys; typed mut initializers. Fixture battery now exercises the scripts from a scratch CWD, catching CWD-relative path bugs.

name: routing-command-node-mechanical-exit
description: Deterministic already-landed preflight pattern (fabro-a32f): a command node with output_schema=routing can route MECHANICALLY without an LLM — the script prints {outcome, preferred_next_label, context_updates} JSON, the engine validates the label against outgoing edge labels, and a conditional edge preferred_label=<label> makes the exit deterministic (the gatebounce node is the precedent; planner-preflight.nu extends it to an exit route). Deterministic tracker writes (closure note then superseded-close) belong inside the script BEFORE the route is emitted, and any write failure must flip the route back to the continue edge so routing and tracker state never diverge.

Stale nextest binary after symlink-path edits: after editing publish.rs via /workspace/fabro (symlink to /repos/denkhaus/fabro), cargo nextest kept failing with an old assertion until 'touch' forced a rebuild. If a nextest result contradicts freshly verified source logic, touch the file and re-run before debugging.
resolution: touch the edited file before re-running nextest when results contradict verified source

name: cross-crate-fork-seam-default-trait-method
description: Cross-crate fork seam via default trait method: when a fork feature needs component-crate classification inside a foundation-crate control path (fabro-core executor cannot see fabro-workflow/fabro-llm classification), add a provided method with a safe default to the foundation trait (Graph::failure_parks_run -> false), override it in the component Graph impl delegating to the fork-only module, and reuse the SAME predicate at both seams (select_edge + executor end path). Upstream behavior stays byte-identical for every other implementor; the fork file keeps the classification; presence pins go in fork-only test files per crate.

Seed fabro-ca1f's 12 failing provider-probe/LLM-path tests all passed on a clean tree (run 01M2QWF2RX4Q0BTB8AQWPH0K4M, 2026-09-17): full fabro-server 956/956 and fabro-workflow 1536/1536 green with zero code changes. The suspected pinned-dep client-side auth drift (lithos-llm/pebble rev bump) did not reproduce — the seed's failure basis had already resolved upstream. Also observed one transient flake: fabro-server cancel_during_startup_persists_cancelled_reason failed once then passed in the no-fail-fast full re-run.
resolution: No fix needed; basis resolved upstream. Seed closed as verified-green.

description: nextest ran stale test binaries after source edits (fabro-4ebd run 01M2R1KKXXG2KZ63F3XT31WT71): two consecutive runs reported union/wire-test failures that vanished after 'touch <test file>' forced a rebuild — the pass/fail verdict came from a pre-edit compiled binary. When a nextest failure contradicts a just-passed isolated run of the same test, force a rebuild (touch the source or cargo clean -p <crate>) before debugging the code.
resolution: diagnosed as stale cargo test-binary caching; workaround: touch the edited source or cargo clean -p <crate> before rerunning; root cause in cargo/nextest fingerprinting unresolved

description: nextest-stale-binary
resolution: diagnosed as stale cargo test-binary caching; workaround: touch the edited source or cargo clean -p <crate> before rerunning; root cause in cargo/nextest fingerprinting unresolved

name: fresh-sandbox-provisioning-from-run-record
description: Ask-Fabro fresh sandbox provisioning (fabro-8d30b): when reconnect of a terminal run's recorded sandbox fails, build a replacement via the spec-based substrate — replacement_sandbox_spec() in lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/sessions.rs reuses the recorded runtime working_directory for LOCAL, and for clone-based kinds derives the DriverSpec from projection.spec.settings.run.environment via sandbox_spec_for_environment with a CloneRequest rebuilt from the recorded runtime's clone_origin_url/clone_branch (repo_cloned==Some(true)), run_id set so OwnedProvider stamps RUN_ID_LABEL. Testing gotcha: Host-provider sandboxes are identified by their designated directory, so deleting the working directory is the Docker-free way to make a local sandbox 'no longer exist' (attach's adopt_directory fails on a missing canonical path).

name: upstream-offer-worktree-shape
description: Upstream offer shape for fork fixes (fabro-b7c4): build the offer in a temp git worktree ("git worktree add /tmp/<dir> -b <offer-branch> <upstream FETCH_HEAD>") created off a read-only fetch of https://github.com/fabro-sh/fabro main, so the main run worktree stays untouched and the implementer verify sees only the loop-asset diff. Port minimal hunks (not fork seam files) onto upstream HEAD, gate helpers cfg(any(test, feature test-support)), verify cheapest-first: rg parse checks, fmt --check, then targeted nextest for the two touched crates with CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the worktree; commit with a Fabro-Run trailer and push the branch to origin denkhaus/fabro via the credential bridge - never open the upstream PR yourself. Avoid backticks in ml record descriptions: the shell executes them inside double quotes.

content: Three nu 0.115 gotchas for loop scripts like planner-preflight.nu: (1) a hyphenated module filename (anchor-check.nu) breaks 'use file.nu <name>' with export_not_found — use underscores (anchor_check.nu); (2) commands imported via 'use' are NOT callable inside sibling top-level defs (resolved as external commands at runtime) — use 'source file.nu' and call the exported defs unprefixed; (3) 'source' is parse-order dependent: defs that call sourced commands must be defined AFTER the source line, and source paths resolve relative to the sourcing file, not cwd.

title: File-schema output_schema applies routing fields alongside output.<node> persist
rationale: Without routing-field application, re-pointing the develop planner to @schemas/planner-output.schema.json would silently strand its preferred_next_label (conditional edges read outcome.preferred_label only) and every planner verdict would fall through to the unconditional Seed claimed edge. Guarding on contains_routing_field keeps non-routing file schemas (gatebounce) inert.

name: fork-only-presence-pin-test-file
description: Fork-only presence-pin test files beside upstream-owned modules (fabro-ec00): move/add the feature's tests into a fork-only fork_*_tests.rs file registered under #[cfg(test)] in the parent mod, and expose the parent's private items with the narrowest seam (pub(super) for items, pub(crate) for #[cfg(test)] helpers inside an exposed pub(crate) test mod) instead of duplicating tests. Applied: server/fork_publish_conflict_tests.rs (new pin), handler/fork_session_provisioning_tests.rs (moved from sessions.rs), server/fork_line_recovery.rs breaker_exemption_pin (moved from automation_scheduler.rs); helper exposure stays cfg(test)-gated per the test-support boundary rule.

title: Graph/engine deploy-velocity skew: deploy the image before flipping graph semantics that depend on new engine code
rationale: Runs clone the repo (graph changes go live with the next run) but engine fixes only go live with a server image redeploy - one PR carrying both halves goes half-live and every run in between fails on the gap

description: Fail-closed SQLite run-history activation is version-sensitive: it replays all run events with the CURRENT projection code and compares against stored terminal rows, so any projection-semantics change (PR #240 quota Failed->Blocked reclassification on 2026-09-18) bricks startup for rows written by older binaries. CI never sees it (fresh DBs). Mitigation pattern that worked: copy prod DB (checkpoint WAL first — cp of the main file alone silently loses un-checkpointed writes), patch rows to the new projection (status column + summary_json lifecycle.status), validate in an isolated container (--network none, dummy SESSION_SECRET, prod settings.toml) until 'Activated SQLite run history' passes, then stop container + backup + patch + start on prod. Era-tolerance precedents live in run_summary_store.rs verify_run_json_field (workflow_version_id 2026-09-05, usage-rename 2026-09-15); seed fabro-eec6 owns the durable fix decision.
resolution: Mitigated 2026-09-18: 4 affected prod rows patched to the new projection (Blocked/quota_rate_limit) after isolated-container validation on a prod DB snapshot; prod healthy again on 0.360.0-nightly.0-15c046bd1. Durable fix (re-projection migration vs era-tolerance vs gate fixture) tracked in seed fabro-eec6.

name: fork-footprint-extraction
description: Fork-footprint extraction pattern (fabro-ab8e): identify fork-added blocks in upstream-churn monoliths by parsing 'git diff <upstream-sha> -- <file>' into contiguous pure-addition blocks with new-file line numbers (python hunk walker, zero-gap merge), then verify extractability with two checks: (a) no outside references INTO the block (its idents unused elsewhere), (b) reverse deps are only helper fns — flip those to pub(super) in the upstream file (precedent: slack helpers for fork_taxonomy_tests). Interleaved rewrite hunks (helpers that exist upstream but appear as + lines, e.g. the pr_test_app region in server/tests.rs) must be skipped — diff line-class lies there; use item-level boundary scan instead. Register new fork files with a #[cfg(test)] mod line next to fork_taxonomy_tests in server.rs. Verify moves-only by #[test]/#[tokio::test] count: tests.rs+fork files before==after.

title: Head-preserving, consumer-resolved preamble output line caps
rationale: Command captures front-load their evidence (integrity headers, seed-work diffs); a tail cap hid the head from summary:high reviewers (fabro-meta-c9f2: 119 lines omitted hid the seed-work diff). Consumer-side resolution matches preamble_inline_max_kb precedence so a read-only reviewer node can raise the cap for evidence it renders.

name: hermetic-provider-env-lookups
description: Hermetic provider-config env seams (fabro-2dac): production honors process env (OPENAI_BASE_URL layers above the [llm] overlay in fabro_llm::build_catalog; VaultCredentialSource::new owns the env fallback), tests must not. Two seams: fabro-server TestAppStateBuilder's default_env_lookup wraps the raw process lookup in hermetic_provider_env_lookup which scrubs OPENAI_BASE_URL; fabro-workflow InitOptions.env_lookup (fabro_auth::EnvLookup) is threaded into build_llm_source -> VaultCredentialSource::with_env_lookup, with start.rs passing process_env_var and every test constructor injecting Arc::new(|_| None) or a controlled map.

name: custom-schema-routing-activation
description: Custom file/inline output schemas are routing-ACTIVE: when the validated payload contains any routing-named top-level field (preferred_next_label, outcome, failure_reason, suggested_next_ids, context_updates), the engine applies routing semantics (apply_routing_fields in lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/structured_output.rs, OutputSchemaKind::File arm ~line 704) even without output_schema="routing". Documented in docs/public/agents/outputs.mdx and docs/public/reference/dot-language.mdx; prompt-lint now warns on routing-named top-level schema properties (nu gotchas: record describe is 'record<...>', and bare (fabro-xxxx) inside an interpolated nu string parses as a command).

content: Fork-specific implementations live in fork-owned files that upstream merges cannot overwrite (fabro-sandbox src/reclaim.rs instead of extending provider.rs; fabro-server src/sandbox_gc.rs instead of wiring logic into serve.rs/server.rs). Upstream files get at most minimal pub(crate) accessors as the seam. Every fork feature is anchored by tests in fabro-server src/fork_seam_test.rs (#[cfg(test)] mod in lib.rs), so an upstream merge that silently drops or breaks fork behavior fails that suite. Test execution belongs to the deterministic tester step; the implementer only compile-verifies (fmt + clippy --all-targets).

Run terminality for in-flight claim detection is proven by the run branch's TIP COMMIT SUBJECT, not the journal's last record: closeout tip = terminal (any status); squash '(#n)' tip = terminal; '(failed)' tip = terminal only past a retry-grace window (the engine retries/bounces failed stages within minutes — observed evidence (failed) then tester (succeeded) in run 01M2RJSBP8). Failed runs write NO journal closeout record (run 01M2WAY0KH's journal ends at evidence), so the journal-last-record hypothesis is false for the failed-terminal case. Secondary: nu interpolated strings treat every bare (...) as interpolation even adjacent to \( escapes — use starts-with/ends-with for paren-heavy match patterns (terminal-tip? in planner-preflight.nu).

description: v0.361 merge (lithos-llm codecs migration): fork-added test fixtures with inline catalogs must migrate with upstream schema changes. node_tools_attribute_narrows_the_wire_tool_set (fabro-workflow it/integration.rs, provider 'compact') still had adapter=openai-compatible + codec=openai-chat; the new catalog loader rejects both (RemovedCodecField). description: Docker sandbox pulls on prod lack registry auth: sandbox containers are created through the host docker API, and API-initiated pulls require client-sent X-Registry-Auth — the host's docker login (fabro-tofu ghcr_auth module) does not apply, and the docker sandbox provider settings have no registry-credential keys. Every private image tag not already present on the host fails on first use with 401 (revisor child 01M2XP626TS98ZTKMR2ZKF4719, 2026-09-19, failed in 336ms pulling ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain:72ea5b4d46e2 after the toolchain env pin). The fabro server image is unaffected (tofu pre-pulls images_to_pull). Interim contract: env PUT + host docker-pull of the pinned toolchain tag are ONE deploy step.
resolution: Workaround landed: merge-upstream skill deploy phase + touchpoints 2026-09-19 now mandate the host pull; product fix seeded for the develop line (registry auth in docker sandbox provider settings)

description: Writing nu (0.115) JSONL parsers for loop scripts hit three pitfalls in run 01M2Y3KA70V33V2SDXXR4921QW (closeout.nu sweep, fabro-22fa): (1) piping into a custom command declared with input signature 'nothing' raises missing_positional — call it with an explicit argument instead of '| cmd'; (2) from json is LENIENT: a non-JSON text line parses to that string, so every where-clause over from-json rows needs a describe-based record guard, not just a null check; (3) str downcase is deprecated — use str lowercase; and string repeat 'x' * n is unsupported — use 1..n | each {'x'} | str join.
resolution: All three applied in closeout.nu/closeout-smoke.nu: explicit-arg calls, describe-based record guards, str lowercase; smoke test green

name: pebble-skill-reference-binding-rule
description: Pebble (pinned rev 67c9f48) expand_skill binds a skill reference ONLY for tokens: '/' at input start or after whitespace + first char ascii lowercase + following chars [a-z0-9_-] + terminated by whitespace or END OF INPUT. Tokens ending at '/', ',', backtick, '*', ')' etc. do NOT bind (/api/v1/* and backticked instances are safe). TWO OR MORE bound tokens fail with MultipleReferences even when both are known. With skills=discover, any UNKNOWN bound token is a structural session killer ('expanding a skill reference', 0 tokens, <1s). Night 2026-09-19/20: 5 develop runs died at the reviewer stage on a single '/install ' inside the RAW fabro-b03f seed description — the planner brief is backticked, but reviewer embeds the raw tracker body. Static prompts are pinned by fork_seam_tests::workflow_prompts_carry_no_expandable_slash_tokens; the tracker-data arm is tracked in fabro-846b.

name: ttft-timeout-at-stream-middleware-seam
description: verify id

When mocking non-2xx fabro API responses in wire tests (httpmock or axum test doubles), the error body entries must include the full ErrorResponse shape INCLUDING the status field (e.g. {"errors":[{"status":"409","title":"Conflict","detail":"..."}]}). A body with only "detail" makes progenitor fail with 'Invalid Response Payload: missing field status', and the resulting error carries no parseable ApiFailure code/detail, so status-branching logic like fabro_client::api_failure_for-based retry-on-409 silently degrades to a generic failure. Observed in fabro-4f44 env_update wire tests (run 01M2ZKNKZVPBN3JM24SQDGVGBT): 409 mock with detail-only body bypassed the revision-race retry; adding status made classify_api_error attach ApiFailure{409} and the retry fired.
resolution: Always emit the full ErrorResponse entry (status+title+detail) in mocked error responses; the wire contract is docs/public/api-reference/fabro-api.yaml ErrorResponse, not a bare detail map.

name: httpmock-json-body-option-skip
description: When asserting a PUT body with httpmock .json_body() against a serde type whose Option fields use skip_serializing_if, the expected fixture must OMIT the key for None (structural equality treats missing != null). Observed in fabro-155b (run 01M2ZSYQR4ZM8N6HD67TT3AT3X): the replace-automation wire test failed with 'Request did not match any route or mock' because the fixture had "description": null while AutomationReplace serializes None as an absent key; also serde RunStatus fixtures need real PendingReason variants (approval_required, not queued).
